# `aitbc gpu-onchain release`

Complete an on-chain GPU allocation (signed GPU_DEALLOCATE, chain v28+). Marks the ``gpu_allocation`` row ``completed`` so the GPU's ``active_allocations`` count drops and the registration can be deregistered cleanly. The signing wallet must be the allocation's allocator or its recorded client; the node refuses anyone else. Before the chain activates state-transition v28 the node refuses the type at admission — there is no off-chain release.

## Usage

```bash
aitbc gpu-onchain release [OPTIONS]
```

## Options

| Option | Type | Default | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `--allocation-id` | text | — | yes | On-chain allocation id to complete (from 'gpu-onchain allocations') |
| `--gpu-id` | text | — | no | GPU id (optional; recorded in the tx payload) |
| `--wallet` | text | — | yes | Wallet name for signing (allocator or recorded client) |
| `--password-stdin` | flag | `false` | no | Read the wallet password from one line of standard input |
| `--password-file` | file | — | no | Path to a file containing only the wallet password (mode 0600, owned by you) |
| `--password` | text | — | no | Wallet password (deprecated: visible in process lists and shell history; prefer --password-stdin or --password-file) |
| `--wait` | flag | `false` | no | Wait for the transaction to be mined |
| `--format` | choice | — | no | Output format |

## Examples

```bash
aitbc gpu-onchain release --allocation-id <allocation_id> --wallet <wallet>
```
